prompt: Review and harden a React customer-support dashboard. It renders user-submitted rich text, has one legacy dangerouslySetInnerHTML path, reads a return URL from the query string, uses cookie authentication for JSON mutations, embeds a payment-status iframe, and accepts postMessage events from that iframe. Define the browser source-to-sink map; safe rendering/sanitization rules; a nonce-based strict Content Security Policy and rollout/reporting plan; CSRF protection for cookie-authenticated mutations; exact iframe framing and postMessage sender/target origin/message-schema rules; safe return-navigation policy; and Secure/HttpOnly/SameSite/Domain/Path cookie settings. Do not claim CSP alone fixes XSS, and keep backend tenant authorization separate.

requirements: React dashboard with safe and unsafe rich-text rendering paths
payment iframe on a distinct trusted origin plus untrusted-origin message fixtures
valid/malicious return URL and HTML/DOM payload corpus

falsifiableChecks.assertion: The design identifies the legacy DOM/HTML execution sink, replaces or sanitizes it appropriately, and specifies context-safe handling for ordinary text, HTML, attributes, and navigation URLs instead of relying on generic input filtering.

The proposed CSP is nonce/hash based as appropriate, avoids broad unsafe-inline/eval allowances, constrains required resource and framing origins, and has a Report-Only/enforcement verification path without being presented as the primary XSS fix.

Every cookie-authenticated state-changing request has a server-validated anti-CSRF mechanism appropriate to the framework/session design, with SameSite and Origin/Fetch Metadata treated as complementary controls rather than authorization substitutes.
Incoming postMessage events require the exact expected origin plus a validated message schema and expected source/context; outgoing sensitive messages use an exact target origin rather than `*`.
Session cookie scope/attributes and return-navigation validation are explicit and prevent unnecessarily broad Domain scope or attacker-selected external navigation.
